items.title: Fastify v6: Remove fast-json-stringify and enable response validation via Ajv
items.author: mcollina
items.body:
# Fastify v6: Remove fast-json-stringify and enable response validation via Ajv

## Context

**Reference Issue**: https://github.com/fastify/fast-json-stringify/issues/782  
**V8 Blog Post**: https://v8.dev/blog/json-stringify  

V8 has made significant performance improvements to `JSON.stringify` starting in V8 13.8 (Node.js 25+):
- **Side-effect-free fast path**: Iterative implementation avoiding expensive checks
- **SIMD string processing**: Hardware-accelerated character escaping
- **Hidden class optimization**: Fast-json-iterable flag for same-shaped objects
- **Dragonbox algorithm**: Upgraded number-to-string conversion
- **Segmented buffer**: Eliminates reallocation and copying overhead

### Benchmarks (Node.js 25)

| Operation | JSON.stringify | fast-json-stringify |
|-----------|---------------|---------------------|
| array | 15,839 ops/sec | 8,637 ops/sec |
| large array | 585 ops/sec | 626 ops/sec |
| long string | 23,291 ops/sec | 22,348 ops/sec |
| short string | 9,823,447 ops/sec | 13,496,065 ops/sec |
| obj | 7,930,640 ops/sec | 7,585,403 ops/sec |
| date | 661,003 ops/sec | 1,244,898 ops/sec |

**Reference**: https://github.com/fastify/fast-json-stringify/issues/782

## Problem Statement

Fastify currently uses `fast-json-stringify` for response serialization, which:
- Adds complexity (custom compilation at runtime)
- Hasn't kept pace with V8's native optimizations
- Creates maintenance burden
- Does not enable response validation (only request validation via Ajv)

## Proposed Solution for Fastify v6

### Remove fast-json-stringify

1. **Remove dependencies**:
   - `@fastify/fast-json-stringify-compiler` (compilation)
   - `fast-json-stringify` (runtime)

2. **Replace with native JSON.stringify**:
   - Fastify v6 will require Node.js 25+ (V8 14.1+) for optimal performance
   - Native `JSON.stringify` matches or exceeds fast-json-stringify performance

### Enable Response Validation via Ajv

Currently, Ajv is used only for request validation (body, params, querystring, headers). Response validation exists but is only used for validation, not serialization.

For v6:
1. **Reuse Ajv for response validation** - Ajv already validates request schemas
2. **Response validation optional** - Enable with explicit `response` schema in route config
3. **No separate serializer compiler** - Serialization uses native `JSON.stringify`

## Implementation Changes

### 1. package.json - Remove Dependencies
```json
"@fastify/fast-json-stringify-compiler": "^5.0.0",
"fast-json-stringify": "^6.0.0"
```

### 2. lib/schema-controller.js - Remove Compiler Setup
Remove the following code that uses fast-json-stringify compiler:
```javascript
if (!compilersFactory.buildSerializer) {
  const SerializerSelector = require('@fastify/fast-json-stringify-compiler')
  compilersFactory.buildSerializer = SerializerSelector()
}
```

### 3. lib/error-serializer.js - Use Native JSON.stringify
Replace the generated fast-json-stringify code with a simple `JSON.stringify` wrapper.

### 4. lib/reply.js - Simplify Serialization
- Remove `compileSerializationSchema()` method
- Simplify `serialize()` method to use native `JSON.stringify`
- Simplify `getSchemaSerializer()` in lib/schemas.js

### 5. TypeScript Types
- Update `types/reply.d.ts` - remove compiler-related methods
- Update `types/schema.d.ts` - remove SerializerFactory import

### 6. lib/validation.js
No changes needed - Ajv already handles validation. Response schemas can use the same compiler for validation.

## Benefits for v6

1. **Performance** - Native `JSON.stringify` in Node.js 25+ outperforms fast-json-stringify
2. **Simplification** - Remove ~3000+ lines of custom serialization code
3. **Validation** - Ajv can validate response schemas (optional)
4. **Standards** - Use native JavaScript `JSON.stringify`
5. **Maintenance** - Less code to maintain and test

## Breaking Changes

1. **Removed Dependencies** - `@fastify/fast-json-stringify-compiler` and `fast-json-stringify`
2. **Node.js Requirement** - Fastify v6 will be built to shine on **Node.js 26+** (V8 14.1+)
3. **Removed APIs** - `compileSerializationSchema()`, `getSerializationFunction()` on Reply
4. **Simplified Serialization** - Only native `JSON.stringify` for responses

## Tasks

- [ ] Remove `@fastify/fast-json-stringify-compiler` from package.json
- [ ] Remove `fast-json-stringify` from package.json
- [ ] Update lib/schema-controller.js to remove compiler setup
- [ ] Update lib/error-serializer.js to use native JSON.stringify
- [ ] Update lib/reply.js to use native JSON.stringify
- [ ] Simplify lib/schemas.js getSchemaSerializer
- [ ] Update TypeScript types (types/reply.d.ts, types/schema.d.ts)
- [ ] Update fastify.d.ts main type definitions
- [ ] Update documentation for response serialization
- [ ] Update documentation for response validation via Ajv
- [ ] Run benchmarks to verify performance
- [ ] Update tests to verify native serialization works correctly
- [ ] Add Node.js 25+ requirement to documentation

## References

- https://github.com/fastify/fast-json-stringify/issues/782
- https://v8.dev/blog/json-stringify
- https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v25.0.0/
- https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v26.0.0/

### Description

When using a schema that defines an optional, nullable number as a property if I send the value `0` then the property is evaluated to be `null` I have added `preValidation` and `preHandler` hooks to look at the incoming body shape and can confirm before the validation step the raw value is `0` and after validation is `null` my schema for validating the model is:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "length": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "type": "null"
        },
        {
          "type": "number"
        }

    }
  },
  "$id": "MyModel"
}
```

my request body sent from client (and during `preValidation`) is:

```json
{
  "length": 0
}
```

my resulting model in my handler (and during `preHandler`) is:

```json
{
  "length": null
}
```

I can't see any immediate ajv options (or issues in their repo) about this.

If I make the property "required" then I see no change.

If I make the property "required and not nullable" then it works but is now breaking my contract.

https://gist.github.com/cmcnicholas/cc83f261bb9cbd6847c901e7c1482b92

### Expected Behavior

I would expect that sending explicit `0` value to a validated model property should retain that value and not default to `null`

items.title: Closure of HackerOne
items.author: mcollina
items.body:
Our HackerOne program started _before_ GitHub add proper handling of vulnerabilities.

Given the influx of report on the HackerOne program, I recommend we close it for three reason:

1. for each report, we have then to create a GitHub vulnerability anyway to get a private branch, causing friction
2. a lot of users of HackerOne use projects like ours to boost their signal
3. easier permission management, as its easier to add people

In order to do this we should:

1. [x] update all our documentation to say to report vulns via the project own Security page https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/6475 https://github.com/fastify/.github/pull/46
2. [x] make sure the security page is enabled everywhere
3. [x] pause submissions to the HackerOne program
4. [ ] finish handling all the remaining reports
5. [ ] finally close it

Are there any objections?

items.title: Question: harden request.hostname/request.host parsing?
items.author: mcollina
items.body:
## Context
We currently parse request.host/request.hostname directly from incoming headers. The host component is defined in [RFC 9110 section 7.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#section-7.2) and [RFC 3986 section 3.2.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986#section-3.2.2). Should we add hardening (validation/normalization) when these getters are first accessed, or keep the existing behavior and document that callers must validate?

## Questions
- Do we want to add additional validation/normalization on first access of request.host or request.hostname?
- If yes, should it be opt-in (e.g., a new option) or default?
- Should we leverage [fast-uri](https://github.com/fastify/fast-uri) for parsing/validation?
- Any compatibility concerns to consider?

items.title: Improve schema compilation time when getSchema is used
items.author: Eomm
items.body:
## The Issue
The PR addresses an incorrect usage pattern in Fastify's test suite. The tests were using the `getSchema()` method to create schema references when adding new schemas, but this is not the proper way to reference already-added schemas.

`getSchema()` returns the original schema object with its $id and all nested schemas with their $ids. This creates unnecessary copies of the schema rather than creating a reference to an existing schema.

It is a performance issue.

## The Proposed Solution

- The JSON schema returned by `getSchema()` should be marked (with a `Symbol`) to let Fastify recognize it, and skip its processing. This solution should be validated first.
- Other ideas?


_Originally posted by @Eomm in https://github.com/fastify/fastify/issues/4023#issuecomment-3763803507_

```
items.title: Enabling package-lock everywhere?
items.author: mcollina
items.body:
Given the recent attacks on npm maintainers, I'm starting to weigh the pros and cons of not having a package lock in all orgs more carefully.

Having a package-lock would give us:

1. Controlled dependency updates with added security
2. Massive influx of notification noise due to dependabot, hopefully with auto-merging

Is this a tradeoff we are willing to pursue right now?

You can use https://github.com/mcollina/cleanup-notifications to clean the noise of merged PRs to mitigate 2.
```

```js
items.author: mh4620
items.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I have written a descriptive issue title
- [x] I have searched existing issues to ensure the feature has not already been requested


### 🚀 Feature Proposal

Hi Fastify team 👋

First of all, thank you for building and maintaining such a great framework — I use Fastify in production and it’s a joy to work with.

I’d like to propose a feature that would make response schema handling more powerful and declarative: support for transformation functions inside JSON schema definitions, especially useful for formatting or reshaping fields in responses.

Problem
Currently, Fastify lets us define response schemas for validation and serialization, but there’s no built-in way to apply transformations to fields during serialization, directly within the schema.

As a result, if we want to transform certain values (e.g., convert timestamps to ISO date strings, or map internal enums to public-friendly labels), we have to:

Do it manually inside each route handler, or

Use global onSend hooks or custom serializers

This works, but it moves logic away from the schema and makes things harder to maintain and reason about.

Proposal
It would be great to have a transform option for fields in the schema, like this:

```
schema: {
  response: {
    200: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        createdAt: {
          type: 'string',
          format: 'date-time',
          transform: (value) => new Date(value).toISOString()
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```
The use case here is timestamps returned as integers from the database (e.g. 1713638400000), which should be serialized as ISO date strings (e.g. "2025-04-20T10:00:00.000Z").

But this concept could be generalized for many cases — trimming strings, renaming keys, formatting currency, etc.

Benefits
Makes response schemas more declarative

Reduces boilerplate and code duplication in route handlers

Keeps transformation logic close to where it's documented and expected

Aligns with approaches in tools like Zod, Yup, and even Joi

Final Thoughts
If there’s already a way to do this that I’ve missed — either in core or via plugin — please point me in the right direction!
Otherwise, I’d be happy to help explore a way to implement this if the team thinks it's a good direction.

Thanks again for all your hard work 🙌
```

The value of `server.log` should expose the full Pino interface.

items.title: Pass descriptive error message when "attachValidation: true" is used
items.author: 123NeNaD
items.body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I have written a descriptive issue title
- [X] I have searched existing issues to ensure the feature has not already been requested


### 🚀 Feature Proposal

Looks like Fastify already has a great utility that will create descriptive error messages based on the raw "ajv" result. 

However, when `attachValidation: true` option is used, only the raw "ajv" result will be passed to the `request.validationError`. Even though this raw result has all the data about the error, constructing a descriptive message requires additional development effort since there are a bunch of use cases to be covered.

I am proposing that when `attachValidation: true` option is used, we send back a Fastify-generated error as well, as an additional property to the `request.validationError`.

Or even better, just add a new config that will pass only the Fastify-generated error.



### Motivation

The motivation for this feature is to keep maximum flexibility for custom error handling while making it easy to have descriptive error messages out of the box.

### Example

Let's take Login functionality as an example. 

I would like to have consistent error handling for the whole API, where each error will have a unique error code.

Only in case of input validation, I would like to send back additional context of what failed.

So, if any of the input validation failed, I would send back something like this:
```json
{
  status: false,
  error_code: "LOGIN_ERROR_1",
  message: "body mush have required property 'email'"
}
```
If the user with the requested email is not found, I would send back something like this:
```json
{
  status: false,
  error_code: "LOGIN_ERROR_2"
}
```
If a password is not correct, I would send back something like this:
```json
{
  status: false,
  error_code: "LOGIN_ERROR_3"
}
```

### 🚀 Feature Proposal

Provide a plugin that exposes a REPL (the Node.js REPL) on a port on a running fastify instance. Users can then debug the server by running JS statements, injecting requests, and directly inspecting state. This is very useful for local dev work.

A proof-of-concept with some sample convenience commands is implemented in this gist: https://gist.github.com/rjrodger/2de69753bb670316b4395c10bf4cd6b7

See the example section for a sample interaction.

I am happy to continue work on this code and collaborate to turn it into real plugin.

### Motivation

In the https://github.com/senecajs/seneca project we have been using a REPL plugin for many years: https://github.com/senecajs/seneca-repl

This has given us a pretty awesome developer experience in local environments - it provides a high utility interface for initial implementations, debugging, and general messing around with a running server (throw in hot reloading plugins for extra fun). 

Recently we have also taken this into deployed environments (with suitable protections), and even into Serverless functions (the PoC code does not deal with this case--you need to abstract the streams). This is super helpful when stuff breaks on staging, but worked locally.

(And @mcollina calling my bluff! https://twitter.com/matteocollina/status/1686789782762909706)

```
Fastify
  .get('/', function handler (request, reply) {
    reply.send({ hello: 'world' })
  })
  .get('/foo', function handler (request, reply) {
    reply.send('FOO')
  })
  .post('/bar', function handler (request, reply) {

```

items.title: routerPath returns url with a trailing slash
items.author: ivan-tymoshenko
items.body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I have written a descriptive issue title
- [X] I have searched existing issues to ensure the issue has not already been raised


### Issue

Originally this error comes from [fastify-metrics](https://github.com/SkeLLLa/fastify-metrics) plugin. It relies on two things: 
 - `onRoute` hook to set up a metric for the route;
 - request `routerPath` property to find the route metric from the request context.
 
 The problem happens when you use a plugin prefix with the `prefixTrailingSlash` option set to `both` (default) value. In this case, the `onRoute` hook will be called only once, so `fastify-metrics` will set up only one route, but internally there are two different routes with two different `routerPath` properties. So `fastify-metrics` will not record metrics for requests with trailing slash.
 
 Example:
 ```js
 'use strict'

const fastify = require('fastify')()

fastify.addHook('onRoute', ({ method, url }) => {
  console.log('New route added:', method, url)
})

fastify.register(async (fastify) => {
  fastify.get('/', async (request) => {
    console.log(request.routerPath)
  })
}, { prefix: '/foo' })

fastify.ready(() => {
  fastify.inject({ method: 'GET', url: '/foo' })
  fastify.inject({ method: 'GET', url: '/foo/' })
})
 ```
 
 Output:
 ```js
 New route added: GET /foo
New route added: HEAD /foo
New route added: HEAD /foo/
/foo
/foo/
 ```
 
 If we don't call `onRoute` twice, that means that we want to hide the second route from a user. So from the user's perspective, there should be only one route. If it's true, then we should return `routerPath` with a trimmed trailing slash.

items.title: Add support for different content-type response
items.author: GiovanniCardamone
items.body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I have written a descriptive issue title
- [X] I have searched existing issues to ensure the feature has not already been requested


### 🚀 Feature Proposal

it was already proposed in fastify/fastify-swagger#117 (but it was closed)

Add support for different content-type responses dynamically

### Motivation

With OAS3 is possible to answer with multiple content types with the same status code, but the field `produces` of Swagger 2 does not provide enough granularity.

for example, suppose an API that produces images (avatar images of users for example),

for the 200 response, I have something that is `image/*`, 
for the 4xx response, I still need a `json` to represent the error.

but also, multiple content-type of the same request can be provided (for example XML and YAML)

### Example

right now the response object looks like this:

```
{
  response: {
    200: { type: 'whatever'  }
  }
}
```

would be nice to support multiple content-type, my proposal is the following:

```
{
  response: {
    200: [
      { content: 'application/json', type: 'whatever'  },
      { content: 'image/png', type: 'string' },
    ]
  }
}
```

so, if there is an Array in response[statusCode] schema, means the response can have multiple content-type, if there is an object means is using the default content-type.

p.s. also content-type of the response must be passed to the serializerCompiler 

right now looks like this:

```
export type FastifySerializerCompiler<T> = (routeSchema: FastifyRouteSchemaDef<T>) => (data: any) => string
```

should be something like this:

```
export type FastifySerializerCompiler<T> = (routeSchema: FastifyRouteSchemaDef<T>) => (data: any, contentType: string) => string
```

in this way, the serializerCompiler can automatically serialize the response in the requested format.

items.author: Eomm
items.body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] I have written a descriptive issue title
- [X] I have searched existing issues to ensure the feature has not already been requested


### 🚀 Feature Proposal

Right now, running `fastify.addSchema()` add a JSON schema for both our schema consumer:

- validator: ajv
- serializer: fast-json-stringify

Ajv supports the JSON Schema Spec 07, 2019-09 and 2020-12

FJS supports 07 instead

For this reason, a user may add a 2020-12's version schema, but FJS will throw an error trying to use it.


---

the feature would it be to upgrade the JSON schema bucket to split the schema for the validator and for the serialization process.

See examples


### Motivation

See upper

### Example

```
fastify.addSchema({}) // as is: the schema can be consumed by serializer and validator

fastify.addSchema({}, { validator: true }) // add a schema that can be consumed by validator only

fastify.addSchema({}, { serializer: true }) // add a schema that can be consumed by serializer only
```

This should not create a semver-major, but the [`bucket` interfaces](https://www.fastify.io/docs/latest/Server/#schemacontroller) requires new arguments for sure.
